conflicts.name: Civil War in Sudan
conflicts.description: What began in April 2023 as a power struggle between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has become the world’s worst humanitarian disaster. The SAF has recaptured Khartoum, but the RSF controls much of Darfur—where attacks on non-Arab ethnic groups have drawn genocide accusations—and has besieged El-Obeid, whose fall would open a direct corridor to the capital.
conflicts.imageAlt: A soldier faces away from the camera while walking on a bridge holding his hand up in a fist.
conflicts.meta: Worsening · Sub-Saharan Africa · Civil War · U.S. impact Low

conflicts.name: Conflict in Ethiopia
conflicts.description: The power struggle between the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and Ethiopia’s federal government reignited following escalating clashes in the wake of the 2020–22 civil war. conflicts.name: Conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo
conflicts.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has been stricken by decades of conflict over its mineral wealth and unresolved tensions from the 1994 Rwandan genocide. Rwanda-backed M23 rebels seized Goma and Bukavu in early 2025 and continue to hold significant territory in eastern DRC despite a U.S.-brokered peace agreement and ongoing Qatar-mediated talks. conflicts.name: Conflict in Yemen and the Red Sea
conflicts.description: Since 2014, Houthi rebels have fought a Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognized government, a conflict that quieted under a UN-brokered ceasefire in 2022. The Iran-backed group subsequently launched attacks on Red Sea shipping in protest of Israel’s military campaign in Gaza, drawing U.S. military retaliation and deepening Yemen’s entanglement in regional conflict. conflicts.name: Conflict With Iran
conflicts.description: In February 2026, the United States and Israel attacked Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and targeting nuclear and military infrastructure. A Pakistan-mediated ceasefire and June MOU halted large-scale fighting, but both sides have since traded strikes over alleged violations. conflicts.name: Criminal Violence in Haiti
conflicts.description: Foreign interventions, political crises, and natural disasters have long destabilized Haiti, a trajectory that worsened sharply after the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moïse. Armed gangs moved to fill the vacuum, seizing control of an estimated 90 percent of Port-au-Prince and displacing over 1.4 million people. conflicts.description: Ethnic and political rivalry between President Salva Kiir and First Vice President Riek Machar has driven South Sudan’s cycles of war since 2013. conflicts.description: Hamas’s October 7, 2023, assault on Israel—killing over 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages—triggered an Israeli military campaign that killed over 70,000 Palestinian civilians and fighters and displaced nearly the entire population of Gaza. conflicts.description: Weak governance, poverty, and climate stress have allowed jihadist groups to establish a foothold across the Sahel, with the Liptako-Gourma borderlands of Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger now accounting for over half of global terrorism-related deaths. conflicts.name: Confrontation Over Taiwan
conflicts.description: China’s claim to sovereignty over the island of Taiwan and President Xi Jinping’s stated objective of “re-unification” by 2049 have driven an escalating campaign of grey zone pressure, including air defense zone incursions and expanding Coast Guard operations. conflicts.name: Confrontation With North Korea
conflicts.description: Under leader Kim Jong-un, North Korea has pursued nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles to guarantee regime survival, posing an acute threat to South Korea and Japan—both key U.S. allies. Kim has deepened ties with Russia, providing artillery and troops for the war in Ukraine, while silencing domestic opposition through mass detention and political purges.

conflicts.name: Civil War in Myanmar
conflicts.description: Myanmar’s military seized power in a February 2021 coup, triggering a civil war that has killed over 100,000 people and displaced 5.2 million. Resistance forces and ethnic armies control an estimated 42 percent of the country against the junta’s 21 percent, though the conflict has entered a stalemate with neither side holding a decisive advantage. conflicts.description: Armed conflict between Muslim Séléka factions and Christian militias has destabilized the Central African Republic (CAR) since 2013, leaving much of the country outside government control. conflicts.name: Conflict With Al-Shabaab in Somalia
conflicts.description: Al-Shabaab has endured as one of al-Qaeda’s most resilient affiliates by exploiting gaps in state authority, clan divisions, and humanitarian crises across Somalia. A 2022 government offensive made early gains but has stalled, with the group deepening ties with Yemen’s Houthis and adapting through guerrilla tactics and counterattacks. conflicts.description: Since October 2023, Hezbollah rocket attacks have displaced roughly 96,000 Israelis from northern Israel, triggering cross-border exchanges and a full Israeli ground invasion in March 2026. conflicts.name: Criminal Violence in Mexico
conflicts.description: Mexico’s narco trafficking organizations have waged a decades-long campaign of violence that has claimed hundreds of thousands of lives, destabilized governance across large swaths of the country, and strained the U.S.-Mexico relationship. conflicts.name: Instability in Iraq
conflicts.description: More than a decade after the self-proclaimed Islamic State’s territorial defeat, Iraq continues to face IS sleeper cell attacks, and over one million Iraqis remain displaced. New Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi faces a September 2026 deadline to disarm pro-Iran militias and convince Washington that Iraq is not beholden to Tehran, a challenge complicated by ongoing U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on Iranian-backed factions.

conflicts.name: War in Ukraine
conflicts.description: Russia’s February 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine has caused more than one million casualties and left Russia occupying roughly 20 percent of Ukrainian territory. Ukraine has countered with long-range drone strikes that have knocked out up to 40 percent of Russia’s refining capacity, while Russia continues to bombard Ukrainian cities.
